name: Kbd
description: An inline keyboard shortcut hint with a raised keycap treatment.

anatomy.description: The raised kbd element sized in ems so it scales with surrounding text.
Plain text between keycaps, like +, keeping combinations readable.

dos: Use Kbd for shortcuts referenced in help, onboarding, or settings copy.
Write platform-appropriate key names, like Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere.
Keep combinations to two or three keys.
donts: Don't use Kbd for user-entered values; use plain or inline-code styling.
Don't style non-keyboard text as a keycap.

examples.title: Shortcut hints
examples.description: Kbd scales with surrounding text through em-based sizing.

examples.title: Combinations
examples.description: Join keys with plain-text separators for multi-key shortcuts.

guidance.useWhen: A keyboard shortcut is referenced in help or onboarding copy.
guidance.avoidWhen: The key is part of a form value; use plain text.
guidance.behavior: Sizing is em-based so the keycap scales with its context.
guidance.responsive: Keep combinations short; wrap groups of keys with separators as text.

notes: Renders a native kbd element, so assistive technology announces the content as keyboard input.
Kbd is purely presentational and takes no focus; it should never be interactive.
